questionText:

"Ibn Battuta was fascinated by plants that were completely unfamiliar to his North African audience. Describing the coconut, he wrote: 'These trees are among the most peculiar trees in the world... "Francois Bernier left a harrowing eyewitness account of the practice of Sati which he witnessed firsthand at Lahore: 'At Lahore I saw a most beautiful young widow, not more than twelve years of age, sacrificed. The poor little creature appeared more dead than alive when she approached the dreadful pit; the agony of her mind cannot be described; she trembled and wept bitterly; but three or four of the Brahmanas, assisted by an old woman who held her under the arm, forced the unhappy victim toward the pyre, seated her upon the wood, tied her hands and feet lest she should run away, and in that situation the innocent creature was burnt alive. topic: Ibn Battuta's Observations on Indian Postal System
questionText: [Set 48.16] In his travelogue 'Rihla', the Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta marveled at the speed and efficiency of the Delhi Sultanate postal system, describing the horse post (uluq) and the foot post known as:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Dawa (stations established every one-third of a mile with swift runners)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Ibn Battuta's Observations on Indian Postal System.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts (Ibn Battuta's Observations on Indian Postal System):
Dawa (stations established every one-third of a mile with swift runners)

Detailed Context:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 History (Through the Eyes of Travellers - Ibn Battuta's Observations on Indian Postal System):
Ibn Battuta observed two kinds of postal systems: the horse post, called 'uluq' (stations every four miles), and the foot post, called 'dawa' (three stations per mile with runners holding copper-belled batons), which conveyed news faster than the horse post.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.
